messages.text: Dad, Ma said the gas bill letter is on the counter. Want me to look at it after work?
I started reading it and put it down before I barked at the paper and the whole kitchen.
Good call. Leave it in the blue folder. I can stop by around 5:40.
Yes. I am telling you now, before I start blaming the pen, the counter, and whoever wrote it.
I'm dropping Mateo's science folder after school. Is it okay if he eats with you and Mom before I pick him up at 7?
Yes, I made extra rice. I will put his folder on the hall table so it does not get mixed with our mail.
Perfect. He has cleats in the car, so don't let him leave them by your back door again 😂
I will watch him. Your mother already moved her shoes so he does not trip coming in.
Leaving the office in 20. Want me to grab milk before I stop at your place?
Yes, and ask Maria if she needs coffee. Elena called about Sunday and Miguel said maybe later in the month.
Got it. I'll be there before 6:30, just across town anyway.
Good. Maria saved you arroz con gandules from yesterday.
I found the old envelope marked Shawmut Ave. There are two photos with Isabel and Rafael on the stoop.
Dad, the wind advisory for Taunton runs overnight. Please do not go climbing around if anything rattles loose.
No ladders. I only put the small toolbox by the back door. If Mrs. Costa's porch latch bangs again I can tighten it from the steps.
That was around South End before we were more over Roxbury. Ma kept those in the blue tin.
That is fine. Call Miguel for anything higher than your shoulder.
One has Titi Ana in the corner too. Should I bring them Sunday so you can write the names on the back?
I know. A loose hinge makes noise all night and then nobody sleeps.
Bring them. I want Isabel to see before she heads back down 95.
I found the scanned card with San Lucas written at the top. The ink is faint, but I can read Ponce and 1949.
Put that one with the recipe pages. Maria says the old papers need plastic sleeves before the kids touch them.
I will bring sleeves Sunday. Do you remember if the photo beside it is before or after the 1956 trip?
After. The one before has Abuela's porch and the mango tree.
The senior center form is on the kitchen table. They want your license copy and that state check page.
I saw it. Mine should be simple. Just the usual old addresses and work dates.
Do not forget to mention the year your sister had all those rides for Luis. They asked about family driving examples.
I remember. She made him sit down with the whole family after that mess and nobody let him shrug it off.
Dad, Mateo forgot his cleats and I have a 9:00 patient check-in. Can you grab him after school if I leave them by the porch?
Leave them there. I will get him at 2:35 and put a plate aside for you too.
You're saving me this morning. He also asked if you still have that little hammer for the loose drawer.
He can hold the flashlight and tighten it himself after we eat.
Dad, I can stop after work if you want me to pick up that lumber from Home Depot.
Leave it for now. The car took enough this month, and the old boards can wait until April.
You sure? I don't mind helping with it.
I know, mija. You have Mateo's sneakers and your own bills. I patched the loose piece for now.
Dad, the town forum is Thursday. They are taking questions on school funding, clinic waits, and the senior center van.
Dad, I found the scan of bisabuela Rosario's baptism paper. It says Ponce, 1912, but the handwriting is hard to read.
Good. I want to ask why the older folks wait so long for rides and why the school aides are still buying supplies themselves.
Mandamelo. I can read the old words better if I make it bigger on the tablet.
Keep it short and practical. Also, please do not put your card into every text link asking for $25.
I'll bring the folder Sunday. There is also a photo from Loiza where everyone labeled only first names.
I know. I gave a little last fall and that is enough for me unless I know the person.
Bueno, we ask your mother too. She remembers who had the Reyes nose and who had my grandfather's eyes.
Fog sitting low by the Somerset stretch. You still bringing the worms or did you forget like the 1998 motor shutdown?
I have them in the garage fridge. Maria put a note on the coffee can so I would not leave without them.
GOOD. I packed the extra thermos. If your knee complains we sit by the ramp and lie about the ones that got away.
You bring coffee and I will bring the folding chair. Same place at seven.
You see that thing Lenny posted? Boiled onion steam fixing everything. Sounds like plant breakroom science.
Found that old break-room photo. You had the blue toolbox open and the line was down again.
Found my old gray rate booklet in the toolbox. Remember the pages for 4 hours minimum if they dragged us in?
Send it. If it was the south line, I probably had the belt laced before your coffee got cold.
I remember. If the press went down at 2:55, nobody made dinner on time.
Leave it alone until somebody who reads the real papers checks it. Those nurses at Sturdy did enough without us passing junk around.
And Ray with the clipboard making sure they wrote the extra hours right. He was a pain but useful.
HA. More like I saved you when the control panel started snapping.
Fair. I deleted my reply. Fishing Saturday if the river is not chocolate milk.
You handled the wires, I handled the belt and gearbox. Same argument since the 70s.
Saturday works. Bring worms, not Lenny's cure.
Useful when the foreman tried to call it regular time.
You still coming by St. Mary's Friday morning? I found the old crew photo with Frank leaning on press 3.
Yes, after the 8:30 Mass. Bring it if you don't mind. I want to ask you the names before I write on the back.
I'll bring coffee. Your knees up for the front steps or should I park by the side ramp?
Side ramp is better now. I am not racing you up church steps anymore.
The flyer from St. Mary's says the ward meeting is Thursday at 6:30. Do you still want me to save it?
Yes. I want to ask why the patrol car keeps skipping Pine Street after dark, and also how complaints get answered.
Write it down before you go. You know you get polite and careful when the room has uniforms.
Old Boston habit. I will bring my note card and keep it short.
Before you disappear out back, the pantry door still catches at the top.
I saw it. I have the plane and the small level on the bench already.
Please put on the clean overshirt Carmen brought if you go to the store after.
This one has the pencil and screws in the pocket. I will brush it off first.
Dad, I checked the city page. The park path lights are still out near the Bay Street side.
Then I will do the morning loop only. My knee complains less when I start early.
Good. Also write down your before-breakfast reading on the days you do the loop, so you can show the office a pattern.
I keep the little notebook by the coffee. The men notice if I skip, so that helps.
Before you go to St. Mary's, put the little crowns in the car. Sister Ana asked if we still have last year's song sheets.
I have them in the folder with the gold ribbon. I will check the loose leg on the coffee table there too.
And call Tía Mercedes after lunch. She wants to know what the notice says about the children's procession.
I will read it to her slowly. Save me two bags of candy for the kids.
The brake shop can do the Toyota inspection repair Monday. They said about $385 if nothing else shows.
Tell them to call before adding anything. I can cover that amount, but I want the month quiet after.
Good. Don't sign up for their payment plan thing. I'll drive you over if you want.
No plan. I will bring the checkbook and skip the hardware store for a while.
Shop called me back. Brakes plus inspection sticker came to $612. You want me to look at the invoice Saturday?
Bring it by. Maria wants it clipped with the gas and parts receipts before she closes the March page.
Ok. Don't pay any extra shop charge until she checks the line items.
Too late for the card, but no more surprises. This month is already looking high.
You still going to the center Tuesday? Eddie says the coffee is worse but they have those town sheets on the table.
I will stop after I get bait. I want to hear what they say about the school roof and that tax number.
Ask Mary at the front desk. She reads every notice like it's a wiring diagram.
Good. I don't like guessing on the names.
Did you use the little case before coffee? The pad by the toaster is blank.
I did it, just forgot to write the number. 146 before breakfast.
Please write it down. Also take the new half tablet with the rest, not later.
Done. I will walk the block after I stretch my hands a little.
Carmen said they will come by around 5:30. Please start the rice before you disappear to the garage.
I am here. Ten minutes with the little speaker while the glue sets, then I will do the sofrito.
And no more turning the volume up when the news bothers you. The neighbors do not need Celia Cruz too.
Fine, low volume. The shelf came out straight, so I am behaving.
Dad, after Mass are you still making the yellow rice with pigeon peas? Mateo keeps asking about the crunchy slices.
Yes, sofrito is already going. I am frying only one pan this time, before your mother catches me.
Good. Put some away before everybody fills the big plates.
I saved containers for you and the kids. Mine gets the small spoon, no mountain.
I sent you the old ship record and the baptism page. Check the message with the subject 'Abuelo notes' when you have a minute.
Dad, for the photo page, is the cap-and-gown picture before or after the one with you holding the Bristol Machine Works lunch pail?
I opened the message. The tree page let me see the names, then it wanted another code and made me start over.
Cap picture first. Lunch pail was that same summer, maybe July. Your grandmother kept saying I could still come home for supper.
Dad, I checked the envelope from Abuela's cedar box. The old church slip says Luis with a 1949 date, but the handwriting is hard to read.
Bring it Sunday if you can. I want to compare it with the picture from Ponce before I write the caption.
That helps. I will caption it simply and leave the longer story for when we sit down Sunday.
Do not start a new account. Use the same one Sofia put on the tablet, and I can sit with you Sunday after dinner.
Put the shop teacher's name if you find it. He was the one who said my hands were better busy than idle.
Good. I found Abuelo Tomas already, so I am not losing that page.
I can. Also please save the sofrito notes you told me in Spanish today, because I only caught half of them.
I will write them slow. Your mother says I talk faster when I remember the old kitchen.
River looks calm by the bridge. You coming or watching those TV people yell all morning?
Coming. I shut the TV off after the hospital story and walked around the block already.
Good. Bring the small tackle box, not the whole garage.
Small box only. Need to clear my head before Carmen calls about Mateo and the car insurance bill.
Lidia called back. She said early July is better than June because Benny's daughter is working odd weekends.
Good. I want days where we sit with people, not run from house to house.
Then we leave blank days between visits. Also no place with a tub only. I am writing that down.
Write down elevator too. My knees will not be brave just because the ocean is nearby.
Papi, I sent you the scan of Titi Rosa's picture. It may look small on your page, but tap it once and it opens bigger.
I saw it. I put the little heart and wrote her name so I remember.
Good. Also the St. Mary's fish supper notice is under events, not in the regular posts.
I will look after the highlights clip Miguel put there. He is still arguing about that ninth inning.
Dad, I checked the Mass.gov page you asked about. It says the newer spring dose is mainly for people your age and to confirm timing with your own doctor.
Good. I will not go by that loud video Joe sent. I want Dr. Rivera or the pharmacist to tell me if March is right.
That sounds right. Bring the Medicare letter too, because it had the coverage note in small print.
I put it with my wallet. Thank you for reading the page without making a big drama.
You still want those tall stakes from my garage?
Yes. The red ones always lean on me by July, and the long green ones need better tying.
I'll drop them Saturday. Need netting too?
Just twine if you have extra. Maria wants the little leaves near the porch kept separate.
Dad, Mateo's school had that presentation today. He said you asked the best question from the back row lol
I only asked if the new officers learn names before they start grabbing kids' backpacks.
He noticed you also asked about the little cameras.
If they wear them, everyone should know when they are on and who checks the tape. That helps the kids and the officers.
You bringing the little table tomorrow or do I have to listen to Luis complain about wobbling again?
I will bring it. Tell Luis the table did not make him lose by 18 last time.
HA. Also if Ray starts on the governor, I am pouring coffee over the score sheet.
No coffee on my sheet. We talk two minutes, then play. Nobody goes home mad.
Ma said you were out with the socket set again. What broke?
Nothing big. Mr. Almeida's handrail had play in it. Two bolts and a shim.
Good. Leave the cellar steps alone until I get there Saturday.
I left them. The rail is solid now though. Bad work bothers me.
Ma said you circled the paving article again. Is that for your folder or are you saving newspaper for the grill?
Very funny. The guy who came to Whittenton last month promised the potholes first, then I see a different number in the paper.
Send me the names if you want. I can check the town page after work.
No, I have it. I just want it straight before I put anything in that envelope for our house.
Dad, Mateo forgot his charger in the back room. Did Isabel use that outlet after the hall dinner?
Yes, she plugged her phone there before the Rhode Island ride. Charger is on the dresser.
Can you keep it there? He may need the couch Friday if practice runs late.
I will tell Maria. The sheets are already washed.
Dad, I found the form for the senior exemption. It asks for the deed book and page from the Bristol County site.
I have the old folder from the closing in the file cabinet. Your mother keeps the tax bills clipped there too.
Bring the folder Sunday. We can scan it and submit it before the city deadline.
Good. After the car work I am keeping dinners simple, so do not let me buy extra for Sunday.
River looks decent Saturday if your knees agree. I found worms, not those fake things you like.
If I bring back even one pickerel, Maria gets the good face at dinner.
You also sent me that Tito Rodriguez Facebook thing at 6 in the morning. Retired men are dangerous.
It came up while I was making coffee. Better than reading repair bills before sunrise.
That mailer came again. Same smiling guy, same hand out. You sending anything?
No. I will vote for the one who keeps hands off the old-age checks and does not blame families who came here to work.
Fair. Frank would have said ask him where he stood when the plant tried cutting the guys' benefits.
Exactly. A speech is cheap. Standing with the workers when it costs something, that tells me more.
Please put the Market Basket slip on the kitchen table, not in your jacket pocket.
I have it. Groceries were $84.37 and gas was $31.10.
Good. With the plant check on Friday and my smaller SSA next week, I want the book clean before Carmen comes Sunday.
I will leave them by your calculator. Don't scold me yet.
Ma said you left early. You taking the cane or being stubborn?
Just the sleeve today. Eddie and Lou keep a slow pace, not like when you drag me through Home Depot.
Fine. Text me after. That corner by the Dunkin gets stupid once school traffic starts.
We turn before that corner. I already wrote the first number down.
I'll swing by Saturday with the drill. Want me to move that folding bed back down from the attic while I'm there?
Yes, only if you have time. Your mother wants the room clear before Elena comes for dinner.
Got it. I'll bring gloves. That mattress is awkward on the stairs.
Thank you. I put the clean towels back in our closet already.
Dad, did the Council call back about that driver thing?
Yes. The woman said my state paper had no marks to explain, so I just need the eye form.
Good. Luis asked me what year Aunt Rosa made him do those Saturday sessions.
Tell him it was long before Mateo was born. Your aunt kept every receipt and every ride schedule.
Dad, Abuela Carmen called me at work again. She got the parish letter and only caught the date.
Tell her I will call at 6:30. Is it the letter about palms and the Friday walk?
Yes. Also they need two people to move chairs after the soup collection Sunday.
I can stay after, but no ladder. Miguel can do high things if they ask.
Dad, I can stop by after work. Need me to grab anything from CVS?
Only the lancets and the refill they called about. Maria says the Monday-Sunday box is low.
Ok. Do you want the soft knee sleeves too, or are the old ones still fine?
Old ones are fine. I need them for the longer walks now, especially past Tremont Street.
Dad, I scanned the plant picnic picture. Do you want me to label Frank and Joe now or wait until Sunday?
Wait until Sunday. Joe remembered three names I had wrong, and I want the story with the machine shutdown right.
Good. Also bring the Medicare letters to the table after dinner. I can sort what is a bill and what is just a notice.
Thank you. I keep them in the blue folder with the recipes and old photos.
Dad, I found two nonstop options from Boston to San Juan. One lands 1:20 pm, the other after 8 pm.
Afternoon. I do not want Maria and me hunting for bags at night.
That also gives you the first evening quiet. I will compare seats near the front and send only the clean options.
Gracias. If we do it, I want to arrive steady enough to see everyone.
Coffee at 9 or are you married to that saw again?
Give me until 10. I glued the last side last night and need to sand before it grabs dust.
Wear the hat with the burn mark so I know you actually did something today.
That hat earned it. I will bring the hinge you asked about too.
Fish won't wait forever. You and Maria coming by the river tomorrow or are the Gonzalez crowd taking over again?
Carmen is coming before lunch, Elena may come Sunday, and Miguel has that furnace job. I will see after Maria checks the calendar.
Maria still running the board like the old plant foreman. Tell Carmen to leave you one free hour.
Joe called the house phone again. I told him you were in the garage looking for the old green cooler.
He worries too much about Saturday. Tell him I found the cooler and the license is in my wallet.
He said no ladders, no heavy cooler, and to let him carry the bucket. For once listen to him.
I will listen enough. He can carry the bucket if he buys the rolls after.
Dad, Carmen said her sink is dripping again. I can swing by Saturday after the New Bedford job if you want me to bring the basin wrench.
Bring it, but let Mateo see the washer first. He should learn why you don't force a nut.
Dad, can I borrow your puller Saturday? Mine is missing the small jaw.
Top drawer, red cabinet. The one with the old number stamped on it still works better than the new ones.
Got it. You want me to grab anything for Ma on the way?
Just milk. I already have Carmen's envelope and the chicken thawing.
Dad, Tio Raul sent me the same screenshot twice. Says don't go near the clinic this month.
Same one you used on the shaft couplings?
Do not forward it to your mother. Send it to Elena first. If it is real, it will be written somewhere better than a blue-background picture.
That one. I kept it after my last punch card went in the drawer.
Good. Carmen said her front desk has been getting calls all afternoon because of that picture.
Then they need fewer phone calls, not more noise from us.
Dad, I can swing by after Mateo's practice if you want a ride to Walgreens. Did they say they have the one Dr. Rivera mentioned?
The pharmacist said they have it but to wait until Monday because of the timing from the office.
Ok. Keep the paper from Medicare in your shirt pocket, not the garage pile.
Yes, boss. Maria already moved it to the kitchen counter.
Sofia says she cleaned up the blue app on your tablet. She left Maria's cousins in there but removed the two names none of us knew.
Tell her I listened this time. I only tapped yes on people with Gonzalez or Rivera and a photo I recognized.
Good. Also, for Uncle Luis at 7, just press the little camera when Sofia calls first.
I can do that. Last birthday I got in before you did.
Found an old break-room photo. You look about 18 and already mad at the stamping press.
That press deserved it. I was still carrying my class ring then and trying not to look lost.
Frank used to say you stayed because Friday envelopes beat sweeping floors at the market.
The envelope helped. So did walking to my parents' place after shift and learning from the older mechanics.
Antonio, the envelope from the retiree plan is on the table. Do not leave it under the grocery coupons.
I saw it. Looks like the same dental card and the March pension paper.
Good. Also Carmen asked if you can pick Mateo up Thursday. Not like the old days when a broken line kept you past supper.
Thursday is fine. Back then one jammed conveyor changed the whole house schedule.
I found the little black-and-white picture you asked about. Is the man by the Plymouth supposed to be Tio Rafael?
Yes, but check the back. If it says Bayamon, that is Rafael. If it says New Bedford, it is your mother's cousin.
Back says Bayamon, 1962. I'll bring it when I come look at the porch light.
Good. I need that one near the page with the pasteles recipe, so the children know whose hands made them.
I'll swing by Saturday for the basement pipe. Don't climb for it.
I won't. I stayed in the garage today and fixed the old lamp instead. Better than sitting with numbers in my head.
What numbers?
Toyota inspection, Maria's refill, and that notice from Blue Cross. I put them in one folder for Carmen.
You still awake? That play at third is going to start ten arguments online.
I was going to bed but now I have to see the last two outs.
I tagged you under the clip. Don't write a whole speech, Ma will blame me.
Only one line. Then I will look at Carmen's birthday pictures and close it.
Mateo counted the candles twice and still got 77. He said next year we need a bigger cake 😂
Tell him I only agreed to the cake, not the arithmetic.
Elena left the copy of the 1956 ticket here. It has San Juan on one side and New York on the other.
Keep it flat in the folder with the Ponce pictures until Sunday.
Papi, Mateo needs help with the interview sheet for school. Can he ask you the questions after dinner?
Claro. He can write my answers the way his teacher wants, but I will tell him the stories plain first.
He wants the one about your abuelo playing cuatro and the other side of the family working near the cane fields.
Tell him bring two pencils. I will mix words if he goes too fast.
Dad, Mateo said you promised him the first red one this year. He is holding you to it 😂
Only if he helps water the back row and does not step on the small pepper plants.
Deal. Do you want me to bring the empty coffee cans for the basil and cilantro?
Bring them Sunday. Your mother already has plans for those leaves.
I saw your note about the faucet. Send me the model number before you buy anything.
No buying today. I found a washer in the coffee can and it slowed the drip.
Good. Just don't crawl under there if it starts fighting you.
I will call Miguel for lifting, not for paying. Tell him that before he starts.
Please do not start another full tray unless Elena confirms. We still have the wrapped ones from yesterday.
I know. I only warmed two and made a little garlic sauce.
And leave the bread on the counter for the others, not beside your chair.
All right, boss. I put my plate in the small blue dish.
Did you move my 10mm socket last Saturday?
No, Pop. Check the red tray by the compressor.
Found it. I was ready to make a big speech at an empty toolbox. Taking five before I touch the Toyota.
Good. Send me a pic before you loosen anything.
Saw you on the community TV replay. You looked like you were fixing a busted press, not talking to the chief.
Same rule, Joe. Good parts stay, bad parts get written up and corrected.
You still brought up walking the side streets after the break-ins.
Of course. Folks should see them before there is trouble, and the rules should be plain after trouble.
The rain stopped. Please eat before you go anywhere.
Just taking the flashlight and checking the two houses by the corner. Mrs. Santos said water came under the back door.
Ten minutes, Antonio. Bring your phone and do not lift anything heavy.
Phone in pocket. If it is only the sweep strip I can measure it and pick one up later.
Do not forget your wooden case after lunch. You left it by the garage sink.
I have it now. Joe says he wants his money back from last Thursday.
Then let him talk less about Washington and count better.
I will keep them moving. If it gets too hot, I ask who is buying coffee.
Found that black-and-white pic you asked about. Rafael wrote Tampa on the back but the front looks like Boston.
Send it to me. If it has Papi by the railing, that was before we moved from the South End side.
Isabel is in it too, next to your mother. Want me to print one for the Florida envelope?
Yes. Rafael keeps asking for copies when he calls.
Do you and Mami need me to stop by after work? I can help sort the mail from the city.
Come if you want coffee. The city bill is the only big house paper now. Maria already wrote the check.
Okay. And please don't buy another tool this weekend just because the car came in under $400 😂
I promised your mother. No tools, no takeout, just rice and beans.
Dad, Carmen sounded worn out when I called. She said she may skip dinner Sunday because the inspection bill hit.
Tell her to come hungry. I will look at the Toyota noise and put something in the glove box after.
She will argue, you know that.
Then Mateo can distract her. I still need him to practice a proper handshake before he asks Mr. Rivera about the summer job.
Dad, the article you sent about the cough medicine was from a sales page. I found the hospital handout instead.
Thank you. Maria said stop reading after dinner, so I put the phone down and said the rosary.
Good. The handout says call your regular doctor only if the fever comes back or breathing changes.
No fever tonight. I will walk in the morning and check on your mother before Mass.
You need me Saturday for that shelf in the garage? Mom said you were moving boxes again.
Yes. I want the top shelf lower. The little wooden cross and Frank's card should not be where I need a ladder.
I'll swing by Saturday. Leave the ladder alone until I get there.
I will. Bring your drill battery if you have it. Mine does not hold long anymore.
Dad, the guy on TV is yelling about cutting waste again. Ma says you are arguing with the screen.
Because they always start with the old people, the clinics, and the schools. Never with the big shots.
Just don't answer those fundraising texts while you're mad.
I deleted them. My money stays for groceries and the grandkids unless there is a local race I truly know.
Papi, the clinic form asks if you had any wages this month. Want me to mark the same as last time?
Same. No checks from anybody, just the monthly deposit.
Ok. It also asks for past job dates. I remember you always say the last year was 2013?
Yes, put 2013. The first badge was from way before you were born.
Papi, the center asked if you can start rides after they finish the last screen. Are you okay with Tuesdays?
Tuesdays are fine. I told them there is nothing old hiding under my name.
Rosa laughed and said she wishes Luis had been that easy when she was driving him everywhere.
She did right by him. Work, home, class, repeat until he understood.
Mateo says Abuelo promised he could hold the flashlight, not the drill. Still true?
Still true. He can mark the line and hand me screws while I tighten the back rail.
Good. Also Mom said you skipped lunch because the little bookcase was being stubborn.
Only one shelf was crooked. I will eat when the glue bottle is closed.
Before Mass, can you look at the article cousin Rosa sent? Big red letters, too many exclamation points.
Send it to me. I will check where it came from and whether anyone local has posted the same guidance.
Thank you. I am not answering her until then. Carmen's office gets enough people worked up over these things.
Good plan. Bring the old photo album tomorrow if you remember.
I found the old photo labels. I can bring them Sunday and sort at the kitchen table after lunch.
Bring them. Maria and I cleared the table after breakfast, so there is room.
Do you want me to bring an extra chair from my car for Carmen if she comes too?
Yes, bring it. The two kitchen chairs are enough for us most days, but Sunday gets crowded.
I can stop by after the supply house. You still want me to fix that frame from the Ponce porch photo?
Yes. The glass is loose, and your mother wants that one on the memoir table.
Is that the little-kid picture or the one from New York in '56?
Little-kid picture. The New York one goes with the ticket copy.
Dad, you still have that laminated lockout card from the plant? Mine at the shop is falling apart.
In the garage cabinet, near the punch cards. We used it every shutdown week.
Figured. You always said the paperwork mattered when someone wanted it done fast.
Fast was fine after the horn at 7, but not with hands inside a machine at 4:30.
Bait shop opens at 7. You bringing coffee or are we both suffering?
Coffee from home. Maria packed egg sandwiches too. No diner stop after that brake bill.
Smart. Those diner eggs cost like they come with a boat.
Exactly. I used the little envelope for the Toyota, so March has to behave.
Antonio, for Sunday dinner please write the menu so Carmen can shop: arroz con gandules, pernil, and the salad.
I wrote it already. I put the notes for her in plain words, but the recipe card stays how your mother wrote it.
Good. Elena also asked if the dark album is your father's family or your mother's.
My father's. The lighter cover is Mami's people from the west side. We keep them separate until I label them.
Antonio, the score is tied again. Please do not start answering every man from New Bedford on your page.
I only answered Joe with the laughing face. I am checking the old salsa video he sent.
Fine, but tomorrow morning I need you rested for the market and Mass.
After this inning I am done. If they leave men on base again I will say nothing.
Dad, Mateo's drop-off is 8:20. Are you still doing your City Hall stop first?
Yes. Your mother and I leave in ten. I put the Sun Chronicle piece in my coat so I don't mix up who said what.
Okay. If the line is long, text me and I'll move Mateo.
No, this is one of the errands we don't skip. The kids and the old folks need somebody paying attention.
River looks decent. You still coming or did the bait bucket insult you already?
Funny. The lid stuck and I almost gave it a lecture.
I am saying it now: give me ten minutes at the dock if I come in hot.
Fine. I will drink coffee and pretend not to hear the first complaint.
Antonio, your arm still sore or are you just trying to get out of carrying the laundry?
A little sore, but fine. The pharmacist said that could happen and Dr. Rivera's nurse said the same.
Good. Elena called and said the state page matched what they told you. I wrote the date on the kitchen calendar.
Thank you. I would rather do it the boring correct way than listen to everybody's cousin online.
Ray says bring the thick score pad today. He claims last sheet robbed him.
Ray says that every time he is down forty.

Mami said you stayed late folding programs. Please don't try to carry those boxes by yourself.

Dad, for the memoir page, should I caption the photo 'Maintenance crew outside Bay 4, 1989'?

Tía Mercedes left me a voicemail about tomorrow's readings. She said you explain them better than the paper.

Scan it. Put it after the picture of Frank holding the broken gear.
I found the city page from 1971 you mentioned. The Grove Hall photo is hard to read, but the street sign is clear.
That was near where we got stopped walking home with groceries. They asked where we were going like the bags were not enough answer.
Do you want that in the family pages, or just keep it for your notes?
Put a small note. It explains why I ask for names, receipts, cameras, and neighbors knowing each other now.
River looks calm. You coming or did the doc turn you into a mall walker?
I can come after breakfast. Have to do my finger stick and take the changed pill first.
Fine, I will get bait. Bring the seat cushion, last time your knees made you curse the dock.
Bring coffee and speak up if the wind is loud. I will do one slow lap before we leave.
You coming for coffee or did another squeaky door beat me?
Coffee after. Mrs. Costa's cabinet hinge is stripped. Whoever put the tiny screws in should be ashamed.
HA. Plant would have fired us for that.
Exactly. I found the right screws in the coffee can. Five-minute job if my knees cooperate.
Coffee after bait shop tomorrow or are you guarding the checkbook again?
Maria has me waiting until she marks the SSA and the pension line. Then coffee.
SMART WOMAN. Mine used to find every missing receipt too.
Tommy asked if you still remember the valve trick from the old boiler room.
Tell Tommy to tap the stem first, then check the packing. Same thing we did before they swapped the compressor.
She found the Toyota one. That is why I am behaving.
He laughed and said nobody on dayshift writes notes like yours anymore.
Those notes kept that place moving from Carter to Obama.
So are you skipping April fishing to go get spoiled by your people?
Not April. Maybe summer if the flights and room behave.
ROOM BEHAVE. You sound like the plant schedule board.
At our age the schedule board keeps you out of trouble. I need a slow week, not a parade.
You left your blue cap in my truck. Again.
Keep it until Tuesday. I am not driving over there just for a hat.
Fine. Tuesday after the hall, coffee is on you. I still say my knot held better than yours.
Your knot held because I showed you forty years ago between shift bells.
Dr. Levin's office called. Your blood work is fine, and he said keep the same walking plan. No new prescriptions.
Good. I was already outside before breakfast. I prayed for Carmen too; she sounded tired last night.
Come in before the coffee gets cold. We will go through the mail together after.
Yes. I left the bank letter on the table so I don't keep opening it by myself.
Please get the smaller pack of chicken thighs. We still have enough for our supper tomorrow.
I am at Market Basket now. I will get the small pack and one loaf.
Good. Carmen said she may come Sunday, so save the big pot for then.
Done. I got coffee too, because we finished the can this morning.
Antonio, I put the envelope with the wedding pictures on your desk. Please do not leave them near your coffee.
I moved the cup. I only need two more pictures before I finish the part about the first apartment.
Use the one where your mother is holding the pot. That is the night she taught me the rice, remember?
I remember. I wrote it the way she said it, with the Spanish words left in.
Antonio, please do not go around the block now. The cars are flying on Winthrop Street.
I know. I will wait for the morning people. My knee is already stiff from the basement stairs.
Good. Put the notebook by your shoes so you do not forget before coffee.
Done. If I miss them, Eddie will call before I finish breakfast.
That cabinet door photo you sent looks level. Did you finally shim the left side?
Yes. Took all afternoon, but it closes clean now. I had Gran Combo going in the garage so I did not throw the screwdriver.
Ma says dinner is loud over there already. Mateo asked if you still have the fish story from Joe.
Tell him I have the story and the Facebook video with the singer in the white suit. Both after we eat.
Dad, Mateo says the Puerto Rican festival flyer is on the community events page. Can you send it to Ma?
I found it. It was under the tomato picture I put this morning.
I saw that. Also please don't stay up too late tonight if the game gets tight. We need you early for lunch prep tomorrow.
I will behave. I already wrote happy birthday to Luis, so I am done on there for now.
Please rinse the tray by the sink before Mass tomorrow. The little green leaves dropped soil again.
I will. I moved them away from the window after supper.
And do not forget the peppers near the basement stairs. They looked dry.
Already watered. The tomato starts can wait until morning.
Dad, thank you for the empanadas. The front desk girls were laughing because you labeled the bag 'for the people answering all the crazy calls.'
They earned them. I saw another cousin post a miracle warning today and closed the app.
Please keep doing that. We had two patients yelling before lunch over something they saw online.
I will ask Elena later. Until then nobody needs me adding more fuel.
We are leaving Bridgewater around 11. Do you want me to bring salad or are you already deep in the pot?
Bring salad. The beans and rice are done, and I made sofrito fresh this morning.
Perfect. I will bring the smaller serving spoon too, since nobody listens once the kids smell it.
Fine, but save me one plantain piece before Mateo clears the plate.
Antonio, before Mass please look at Elena's message. She says the old census page is ready to save.
I saved it after the second try. The little box kept saying my word was wrong, so I used the reset from my mail.
Good. And do not forget Sofia is calling at 5 so you can practice before your brother's family joins.
I know. I put the tablet by the lamp where the picture is not so dark.
The coupon drawer is messy again. Please do not start pulling everything out before Elena comes.
I already shut it. The receipt printer at Shaw's beat me today.
Then sit with your coffee. We can find the coupon together after Mass.
That is why I told you. I could feel myself about to argue with a drawer.

events.title: St. Mary's early setup, 9:30 service, pantry boxes
events.notes: Bring folding tables, blue tape, small screwdriver, canned beans. Ask Doña Luz which envelopes need the wording read back before she signs.

events.title: Coffee, finger check, new AM pill
events.notes: Use green case before breakfast. Write number on kitchen pad. Short walk after dishes if knees are okay.

events.title: Walk at Hopewell Park, then stop at St. Mary's
events.location: Hopewell Park, Taunton; St. Mary's Church
events.notes: Before news comes on. Bring rosary. Ask Maria about the electric bill envelope after coffee.

events.title: Hopewell Park loop with rec center walkers
events.notes: Wear gray knee sleeve. Log morning number before breakfast. Avoid Bay Street crossing if cars are backed up.

events.title: Precinct 4 stop before breakfast
events.notes: Bring blue folder from kitchen drawer. Check Sun Chronicle clipping with road paving list and senior van hours before marking the sheet.

events.title: Market stop before lunch prep
events.notes: Green plantains, pigeon peas, cilantro, culantro, garlic, onions. Cook one pot only; use the small scoop for my plate and freeze extra.

events.title: Bank and receipt folder
events.notes: SSA posts today. Bring blue folder for Maria; check Toyota repair line before moving anything from savings.

events.title: Gutter flashing estimate
events.notes: Ask if the small section can stay near $400. Use checking if needed. No store card.

events.title: Flatbed scanner and blue binder
events.notes: Shoebox #2: write names on sticky notes first. Add arroz con gandules card behind the photo of Tia Luz's kitchen.

events.title: Garage bench, plane irons, phone speaker
events.notes: Put Hector Lavoe queue on low, sharpen two irons, check saved Facebook videos after cleanup if the shelf glue is dry.

events.title: Tablet with Tia Rosa and cousins
events.notes: Charge tablet after supper. Open the link Carmen sent. If it asks again, use the six-number code before it expires.

events.title: Maple St walk: Costa latch, Santos window
events.notes: Bring Phillips driver, WD-40, flashlight. Knock first; back by 9 for coffee with Maria.

events.title: Sort old papers for Elena
events.notes: Look for Class of '68 photo, first Bristol Machine Works badge, union card, and the envelope from Mom's house on Bay Street.

events.title: Call Titi Lidia about July dates
events.notes: Ask which cousins will be around. Check if the spare room is still upstairs or if the downstairs room is open.

events.title: Back beds: turn soil, set old cages
events.notes: Check twine, labels, and the bags by the shed before breakfast.

events.title: Call Dr. Rivera's office about March dose
events.notes: Ask whether Walgreens on County St. or the office clinic is better. Keep Medicare card nearby and write down what the pharmacist says.

events.title: Back table with Joe and the guys
events.notes: Bring score pad, quarters, and the wooden case. Keep State House talk before the first shuffle.

events.title: Ward 3 meeting at library
events.notes: Ask about Pine Street evening car, posted camera-use rules, complaint follow-up letters, and more walking introductions near St. Mary's.

events.title: Game on NESN after supper
events.notes: Check St. Mary's notice on the blue app first; Maria asked for cousin Lidia's new photos to be saved before first pitch.

events.title: Mass at St. Mary's, then coffee with Joe
events.notes: Bring Frank's prayer card, plant photo envelope, and cane. Ask Joe about the two men near the boiler room door.

events.title: Drop off volunteer driver packet
events.location: Taunton Council on Aging, 30 Olney St
events.notes: Bring license copy, sealed state check receipt, and two references. Add short note about helping Luis get to work while his license was held years back.

events.title: Update house key ring
events.notes: Check front and back door copies. Keep Antonio and Maria tags on the hooks; put Carmen's spare in the blue envelope before she stops by.

events.title: Coffee with Joe after benefits office talk
events.location: Taunton Council on Aging, 30 Olney St
events.notes: Bring printed questions: retiree checks, clinic paperwork, old plant pension forms. Do not sign up for recurring card charge at the table.

events.title: Morton Hospital front desk stop
events.notes: Drop Maria's thank-you card and two bakery boxes. Keep the forwarded clip for Elena to look at before replying to the cousin thread.

events.title: Rice, beans, sofrito; Mateo tomato tray
events.location: Home kitchen and back steps, Taunton
events.notes: Start beans before Mass clothes. Save Carmen two containers. Show Mateo the seed spacing before lunch; Maria wants the porch rail checked after dishes.

events.title: Sunday table: Maria, Elena, Carmen, Miguel maybe
events.notes: Make pernil early. Carmen can bring rolls from Broadway; Elena coming from Bridgewater if the roads are clear. Ask Miguel about the porch rail.

events.title: Cut boards for hallway seat; check loose drawer runner
events.notes: Safety glasses, clamps, 80-grit paper. Leave room to park before Maria gets back.

events.title: Sort family memoir photos with Elena
events.notes: Set aside albums marked Ponce, Mayaguez, and Loiza. Ask Maria about Abuela Carmen's recipe cards; add captions in both columns before printing.

events.title: Fresh sheets: back room
events.notes: Isabel after St. Mary's hall dinner. Leave air mattress folded in closet in case Mateo stays too.

events.title: TRA monthly sign-in with Joe
events.location: Taunton Eagles hall, 29 Oak St, Taunton
events.notes: Bring renewal envelope, small tackle box for swap table, and the printed river cleanup sheet.

events.title: Blue folder before coffee
events.notes: Open bank notice with Maria. If the numbers do not add up, call Carmen before sorting tools or mail.

events.title: Garage shelf: sort old shop binders
events.notes: Keep the pump seal chart, air-line fittings list, and motor tag notebook. Ask Maria about the box marked 2013.

events.title: Market Basket sale run + freezer check
events.notes: Use coupons from drawer. Beans, rice, chicken thighs if marked down. Check freezer before buying more. Leave hardware aisle for another week.

events.title: Call Local 318 retiree office
events.notes: Ask about pension deposit notice and whether the old safety shoe reimbursement form still matters for retired members. Have plant ID and last 7:00-3:30 timecard copy nearby.

events.title: Thursday table
events.notes: Coffee money in jacket. If mayor talk gets loud, switch seats and start next hand.

events.title: Dinner at Carmen's - cake, old photo envelope
events.notes: Bring the Ponce envelope, the San Juan-New York ticket copy, and the candles Carmen bought.

events.title: Walgreens County St. counter
events.notes: Bring Medicare notice. Ask pharmacist to compare it with Dr. Rivera's message before agreeing. Text Elena if the wording is confusing.

events.title: Coffee table talk at senior center
events.location: Taunton Council on Aging, 30 Olney St
events.notes: Ask about people on the town list: property bill change, school buses, Council on Aging lunch schedule. Bring folded Gazette page.

events.title: Meet Eddie, Lou, and Fran by rec center bench
events.location: Taunton Council on Aging parking lot
events.notes: Two laps if knee feels steady. Bring water and reading notebook. Stay on the river side, away from Broadway traffic.

events.title: Prep pernil and arroz con gandules
events.notes: Charge speaker before chopping. Elena bringing photos. Open Facebook saved post from Nydia only after the pork is in.

events.title: Carmen stop-in: groceries and mail
events.notes: Leave checkbook on kitchen table for Maria. Ask Carmen about Mateo ride Friday. Save leftovers if Elena calls.

events.title: River morning - Joe driving
events.notes: Pack chair, thermos, two rods, bait receipt, and the blue association cap.

events.title: Dr. Patel follow-up
events.notes: Bring meter, kitchen pad, cuff card, pill bottles, and the small ear pieces. Ask about the changed dose and walking goal.

events.title: Library printer: binder pages
events.notes: Print draft pages 6-10. Check spelling for Gonzalez names. Leave blank space beside recipe story from Maria.

events.title: Check 10-day pill boxes before ticket hold expires
events.notes: Count morning and night rows. Ask pharmacy about extra labels for carry-on bag.

events.title: Kitchen-table numbers with Maria
events.notes: Normal target: $3,100-$3,300. March rough count: $3,700 because of Toyota. Talk before pulling from savings.

events.title: Pick up copies at Taunton Historical Society
events.location: Old Colony History Room, Taunton Public Library
events.notes: Ask for 1968 yearbook scan, Bristol Machine Works apprentice-program clipping, and city bus map from Bay Street to the plant gate.

events.title: Move porch pots outside if warm enough
events.notes: Check overnight temp first. Pinch basil tops, thin pepper tray, water cages by fence.

events.title: Open Sofia's link before Aunt Lidia comes on
events.notes: Tablet plugged in. Check email first for the new link. Do not press confirm on names Sofia did not circle.

events.title: St. Mary's: 9:30 service, repair closet latch, canned goods table
events.notes: Bring pliers, extra labels, grocery bags. Call Tío Rafael afterward about the bulletin times for Thursday night and Friday afternoon.

events.title: Sunday pot and containers
events.notes: Mofongo for visitors; keep fried pieces on paper towels. Set aside two small containers before serving. Skip second roll at table.

events.title: Pick up 1x6 pine, cabinet pulls, and sandpaper
events.notes: Use old jacket with deep pockets; measure kitchen corner twice before cutting.
